author: WP01
summary: The house-style chapter: match FNA/XNA exactly, two namespace families, the CNAEXT marker and its strict check, property/alias/event/interface/IDisposable/visibility translations, module layout, no shims, Doxygen, missing dependencies and the per-file checklist. It is alpha.1-era text never re-synchronised: examples drifted (Color has no GetTypeName, SkinnedEffect throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, header counts, ReadChar semantics, XNA-wins rule). The site's conventions page had the rules and how they are held; the worked examples, the translation reasoning and the drift between written rules and code were missing and are on the new conventions page.

concepts.section: Language, Conventions, and CNAEXT
concepts.text: CNA enforces its conventions through its CLAUDE.md porting rules and CHECKLIST.md, and every code example assumes them.

concepts.section: The prime directive: match FNA, not taste
concepts.text: The porting rules name a local FNA source tree as the single behavioural reference and forbid treating old CNA code or AI-generated stubs as authoritative when they conflict with it.

target.evidence: CLAUDE.md: still true, but since the 2026-09-04 owner decision measured XNA wins where XNA and FNA disagree

concepts.section: The prime directive: match FNA, not taste
concepts.text: Class, struct, enum, method, operator and constant names match XNA/FNA exactly; nothing is renamed to look more C++-like.

concepts.section: The prime directive: match FNA, not taste
concepts.text: Behaviour beats preference: packed layouts (Color as AABBGGRR), clamping, casts, operators, overloads, defaults and exceptions follow the reference.

concepts.section: The prime directive: match FNA, not taste
concepts.text: C++ member order mirrors the C# source order where practical so review can diff against the reference.
tokens: Member order mirrors the C# source

concepts.section: Two namespaces, two jobs
concepts.text: Real XNA types live in Microsoft::Xna::Framework and are never moved into CNA; project extensions, helpers and back ends live in CNA; anything non-XNA inside the XNA namespaces must be marked.

concepts.section: The CNAEXT tag: a compiler-enforced honesty check
concepts.text: CNAEXT is an empty marker macro in modules/core/include/CNA/CNAHelper.hpp that tags a declaration inside the XNA namespaces as not part of XNA 4.0.

concepts.section: The CNAEXT tag: a compiler-enforced honesty check
concepts.text: Example: Color's real Equals(const Color&) is unmarked while a CNA-only GetTypeName() override in the same class is marked CNAEXT.
concepts.note: The example is stale; the catalogue lists Color's real extension members.

target.evidence: modules/math/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Color.hpp: Equals(const Color&) override (IEquatable); Color declares no GetTypeName; its marked members are the byte constructors, operator*(float, Color) and getDebugDisplayStringProperty()

concepts.section: The CNAEXT tag: a compiler-enforced honesty check
concepts.text: CNA_STRICT_XNA_API makes CNAEXT expand to [[deprecated("CNAEXT: not part of the XNA 4.0 API surface")]]; it is never set for the CNA library and is scoped to two standalone targets in cmake/Harnesses.cmake compiled with -Werror=deprecated-declarations.

concepts.section: The CNAEXT tag: a compiler-enforced honesty check
concepts.text: The check verifies itself: a positive target compiles StrictXnaApiSurfaceCheck.cpp avoiding every marked sensor member, and an EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL negative target that calls InjectSyntheticSensorUpdate is built by a WILL_FAIL TRUE CTest, so a broken guard turns the test red.

concepts.section: C# properties, translated consistently
concepts.text: C# auto-properties become a getXProperty()/setXProperty() pair, never a public field unless the type already uses fields.

concepts.section: C# properties, translated consistently
concepts.text: A validating C# setter keeps its logic: SkinnedEffect::setWeightsPerVertexProperty rejects anything but 1, 2 or 4 (std::out_of_range) and sets a dirty-shader flag so the next Apply selects a new variant.

concepts.section: SharpRuntime type aliases: never a raw C++ primitive in the XNA surface
concepts.text: C# primitives map to sharp-runtime aliases (bytecs/Byte=uint8_t ... charcs=char16_t, Single=float, String=std::string) so the XNA surface keeps a greppable link to .NET.

concepts.section: SharpRuntime type aliases: never a raw C++ primitive in the XNA surface
concepts.text: A missing alias is added to sharp-runtime first, never replaced by a raw C++ type in the XNA surface.

concepts.section: Events, as System::EventHandler<T>
concepts.text: C# events use System::EventHandler<T> uniformly: a field declaration, += with a (sender, args) lambda, and Raise/Invoke.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Game.hpp (EventHandler<System::EventArgs> Exiting, not ExitingEventArgs); sharp-runtime@41b918c9 EventHandler.hpp (Add returns Token, Remove(Token), no operator-=)

concepts.section: Interfaces as abstract base classes, IDisposable as a pattern
concepts.text: C# interfaces become abstract base classes (Color implements IPackedVectorT<UInt32>); a deviation from an exact mapping is explained in the change description, not in a source comment.

target.evidence: Color.hpp at TARGET also derives from System::IEquatable<Color>, which the rule's example omits

concepts.section: Interfaces as abstract base classes, IDisposable as a pattern
concepts.text: IDisposable maps to System::IDisposable with Dispose() and optional Dispose(bool); an isDisposed_ guard precedes every operation and use after dispose throws std::runtime_error.

target.evidence: CLAUDE.md still says std::runtime_error; modules/graphics/src/Xna/*.cpp throw System::ObjectDisposedException (69 occurrences), e.g. SpriteBatch.cpp

concepts.section: Visibility is chosen, not defaulted
concepts.text: C# internal members become private, protected, detail-namespace or omitted, never public by default; an internal DebugDisplayString must not become public API.

target.evidence: Nine math/geometry types keep getDebugDisplayStringProperty private; Color exposes it publicly, marked CNAEXT

concepts.section: Physical modules own the namespace-shaped include surface
concepts.text: Each physical module owns declarations under modules/<owner>/include and implementation under src; the include subtree mirrors the namespace while implementation paths use a shorter area directory.

concepts.section: Physical modules own the namespace-shaped include surface
concepts.text: The Graphics include subtree holds 125 headers: 107 directly in the Graphics directory and 18 in PackedVector.

target.evidence: At 009d40f5: 115 + 18 headers in modules/graphics and PackedVector/IPackedVector.hpp in modules/math = 134

concepts.section: Physical modules own the namespace-shaped include surface
concepts.text: Non-template implementations do not live in headers.
tokens: Non-template implementations do not live in headers

concepts.section: No backward-compatibility shims
concepts.text: Correcting an API never adds a compatibility alias for old call sites; old demos are fixed instead (wrong: a free inline CornflowerBlue; right: Color::CornflowerBlue).

concepts.section: Documentation: full Doxygen, or nothing
concepts.text: Every public declaration needs a full Doxygen block, never a bare ///; C# XML doc intent is kept, often verbatim from FNA, but never labelled 'taken from FNA'.

concepts.section: Missing dependencies: stub correctly, never invent
concepts.text: A missing .NET type is added to sharp-runtime; any other missing type gets a minimal correctly named stub in its final namespace, and every stub is reported in the task description.

concepts.section: Missing dependencies: stub correctly, never invent
concepts.text: Worked example: BinaryReader::ReadChar()/ReadDecimal() were missing in sharp-runtime; ReadChar() now decodes one UTF-8 code point and throws FormatException for invalid bytes or for a code point above 0xFFFF, matching .NET.
concepts.note: The supplementary-plane case no longer throws; the page states the current behaviour.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime@41b918c9 modules/io/src/System/IO/BinaryReader.cpp (TryReadChar returns the high surrogate and queues the low one for a scalar above 0xFFFF); ReadChar added in commit 4cbf00db (2026-07-16)

concepts.section: Missing dependencies: stub correctly, never invent
concepts.text: The interim workaround was a diagnostic-quality stopgap patch preserved in the book's own screenshot infrastructure materials.
concepts.note: Book-internal tooling history; no current CNA fact.

concepts.section: The per-file porting checklist, in miniature
concepts.text: The per-file minimum: SPDX MS-PL headers in .hpp and .cpp, CNAHelper.hpp included when CNAEXT is used, line-by-line comparison with FNA with deviations commented, GetTypeName() overridden and marked with the fully qualified name, and a unit test per public method (out/ref overloads and static factories separately).

concepts.section: The per-file porting checklist, in miniature
concepts.text: A file is completed in one pass; the checklist rejects deferring items to a later, unscheduled pass.

concepts.section: Why this chapter earns its place in a ``bible''
concepts.text: The conventions matter together because they keep a large multi-renderer codebase auditable against external references at every layer, turning a non-XNA leak into a build error rather than a review catch.
